name: Bike Lane Memorial Sculpture
address: 3216 Bloor Street West (nearest address), Etobicoke, Toronto, ON M8X 1Z4
artist_attribution: Community members (individuals not named in coverage)
description: Pyramid of red-painted bicycles attached to a utility pole, erected overnight in October 2026 as a protest memorial during the provincial removal of protected bike lanes on Bloor Street West. Each bicycle represents one of 32 people killed on Bloor Street, Yonge Street and University Avenue between 2000 and 2020, before bike lanes were installed (21 pedestrians, 4 cyclists, 3 motorcyclists, 4 drivers).
notes: Not in any zone: the site is at Bloor and Islington in Etobicoke, outside the downtown zones, so zone and sub-zone are left blank. Coordinates are for Tom Riley Park (from touristplaces.ca), not the exact spot of the sculpture; address is the park's nearest address per Toronto Nature Stewards (another site lists 3219). Temporary protest installation: confirm it is still in place and whether it should stay on the map. Accessibility not yet checked.
